description: Every machine NASA left behind has a story. This solo project brings those forgotten heroes back to life - the rovers, landers and tools left on the Moon and Mars. Through interactive storytelling, I turn abandoned equipment into unforgettable characters, so people can explore, feel and remember what they left behind.
summary:
Left Behind, Never Forgotten tells the stories of NASA's machines left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware behind - not as trash, but as explorers that taught us how to explore.

We tell the stories of Apollo hardware on the Moon, Spirit which lasted 24x longer than planned, Opportunity which drove 45 km over 14 years, Ingenuity which flew 72 times instead of 5, and Voyager 1 and 2 which are still talking to Earth from interstellar space.

Through storytelling, numbers and a quiz, we show these machines are abandoned but not forgotten. Their data still helps build the next rovers and spacecraft. By Team One Man Mission.
details: Left Behind, Never Forgotten is a digital storytelling and memorial project created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by Team One Man Mission. What does it do / How does it work? Our project tells the story of NASA's Opportunity Rover and all the machines we have left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in space. It is a 6-page interactive digital presentation that combines real NASA mission history, emotional storytelling, and visuals to make people feel connected to these robots. Users scroll through the journey - from launch, to exploration, to the final signal, to the legacy they left. It works as a web / PDF experience that anyone can open on mobile or desktop, no app install needed. What benefits does it have? 1. It preserves space history in a simple, emotional way for students and the public. 2. It makes complex NASA science easy to understand for non-scientists. 3. It inspires young people in India and around the world to learn about space, robotics, and STEM. What is the intended impact? We want people to stop seeing rovers as just machines, and start seeing them as explorers who sacrificed themselves for human knowledge. Our impact is to increase public interest in space missions, encourage students to follow NASA missions, and create a new way to remember missions that are no longer active. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did we use? We used Canva and Google Docs for design and storytelling, Google Drive for sharing, mobile phone for complete development, and NASA open data / mission archives for research and facts. No heavy coding was needed - the focus was on design, storytelling, and accessibility. How is our project creative? Instead of making a normal science report, we made it a memorial - like a tribute. We used the famous last message of Opportunity, "My battery is low and it's getting dark", as the emotional core. The design uses dark space, Mars red, and Moon light to create a cinematic feeling. It is science + emotion + art together. What factors did our team consider? We considered accessibility - it must work on low internet and mobile phones. We considered accuracy - all mission facts are based on NASA sources. We considered audience - students, general public, and judges who may not be scientists. And we considered emotion - a project people will remember, not just read. Our message is simple: Machines may be left behind, but their discoveries are never forgotten.
